question.problem:
The manager wants to determine the number of wooden tables the company should produce per week to make a weekly profit of $$4\,800.$ The required number of wooden tables $x$ is the solution to the equation

$$
6{x}^{2}-360x+4\,800=0.
$$

This equation can be factored as $\,$

                                         $)=0.$
question.worked_solution:
We factor $6{x}^{2}-360x+4\,800$ using the greatest common factor (GCF).

Computing the GCF, we get

$$
\text{GCF}(6{x}^{2},360x,4\,800)=6
$$

Then, we rewrite each term in the original expression as a product with the $\text{GCF}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}-360x+4\,800 & = \\ 6\cdot ({x}^{2})+6\cdot (-60x)+6\cdot (800)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the $\text{GCF}$ outside the parentheses and keep the remaining terms inside:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot ({x}^{2})+6\cdot (-60x)+6\cdot (800) & = \\ 6({x}^{2}-60x+800)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is ${x}^{2}-60x+800.$
